The comparative case study examines top-down and bottom-up governance arrangements for flood risk management within Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) in Catalonia and the San Francisco Bay Area, with no examination of household or community drinking water or sanitation service access or access outcomes.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both readings result in exclusion (E07) because the study examines flood risk management and river-basin/regional IWRM rather than household or community water supply or sanitation service access, even though institutional governance arrangements are analysed under the plain Criterion 2 wording.

evidence_quotes.quote: Flood risk management in the context of Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) is becoming widely accepted as an approach to improving resilience in light of increasing flood risks due to climate change and other factors.
This paper contributes to a better understanding of the governance arrangements needed for effectively implement integrated approaches to managing flood risk.

The European Union's top-down approach and the presence of a central authority at the river basin scale have led to a consolidated regional plan in Catalonia encompassing all phases of flood risk management
